reason: Driven end to end and reproduced exactly. state=owner-empty -> type '3 October 2026' -> Set the day -> Add a moment, at 1440x960: .b-measure is 1514px tall at 18px/day, holds ONE .b-item at data-away=40 whose box ends at 799px, and 715px of bare .b-rail runs below it to nothing. Zero elements carry data-anchor="true". Scrolling the .b-plan pane to its foot (scrollHeight 1565, client 664) with the fixed horizon still in place shows the whole right column as one unbroken hairline with no mark, no row and no terminus on it. Not a desk-only artefact: at 390x844 the built plan is 1198px with a 567px empty tail, and pressing Preview - the artifact the audience actually receives - gives the guest 1198px with a 591-599px empty tail and one row. The seeded fixture hides it exactly as the finding says: fixture.js line 87 carries a 'Wedding day' milestone on 2026-10-03, which is also PROJECT.primaryDate.date (line 95), so every graded frame terminates on a data-anchor row with a ~35-53px tail (owner-flight 1536/tail 35, desk 1198/45, phone 1040/53). The measure's own code confirms the intent rather than contradicting it: place() sizes the rail to daysFrom(clock, F.project.primaryDate.date) * px + ROW, so the rule is already drawn all the way to the day and simply says nothing when it gets there. Strongest evidence that this is a defect and not taste: the behaviour gate itself asserts the invariant the built plan breaks - interaction-check.mjs line 238 'the horizon count is the last item on the measure' and line 239 'exactly one item is the day itself' - and asserts it ONLY against the seeded state=phone. On the plan a real first owner builds, the horizon count is 79 and the last item is 40, and the anchor count is 0. So this is not a restatement of a gate; it is an unasserted state in which two of the gate's own stated laws are false. Scope: the fix is design, not schema. F.project.primaryDate already exists on the record and is already rendered three times on the same surface (the 96px count, the ceremonial date, the .b-sub label) and already governs the editor's ceiling refusal 'This is as far as it goes. <label> is the last day.' Deriving one terminus row from a field the renderer already reads introduces no new field and no data-model change. It breaks no non-negotiable: hairline at --fore-28, hollow tick, weight 600 - all already in use on .b-item[data-anchor="true"]. Nor would it make the composition worse by repetition: the accepted seeded plan ALREADY states the day both as .b-sub and as the last row of the measure, in the same viewport at desk width, so the fix makes the built plan consistent with the frame the panel has been grading, not noisier than it. The one real flaw in the fix as written is 'always append', which on the seeded plan would render 'Wedding day' twice on 2026-10-03 and trip the stacking path into 'first of 2 moments on this day' - repairable with one guard, sharpened below.
sharpenedFix: In render-b.js measure(), after the ahead() rows are pushed, append a terminus row ONLY when no milestone already sits on F.project.primaryDate.date - otherwise the seeded fixture, whose 'Wedding day' milestone IS the primary date, renders the day twice and stacks it as 'first of 2 moments on this day'. Build it through row() so its geometry is identical, positioned at daysFrom(clock, F.project.primaryDate.date), titled F.project.primaryDate.label with the same weekdayShort + short dateline, carrying data-anchor="true" so it inherits the existing full-width hairline, hollow tick and 600 weight with no new CSS. Mark it data-terminus="true" and treat it as the project's day rather than a moment: no .b-grab (it is not editable, and the editor's ceiling refusal already names it), excluded from the moment count in the bar, from the gap note's nearest-item sentence, from the 'Behind you' record, and from every editor target and stepper collision path. Its accessible unit should read as the day, not 'days away' - e.g. ' days away, the day itself,' - so a screen reader hears why the list ends there. Then move interaction-check.mjs's two invariants off the seeded fixture and onto the built plan as well: after the owner-empty -> Set the day -> Add a moment path, assert that the horizon count equals the last row on the measure and that exactly one row is the day itself. Those are the assertions that currently pass only because the demonstration fixture happens to carry the day as a milestone. Note the existing round-6 assertion 'the first action puts a moment on the plan' counts .b-item and will need to count :not([data-terminus]) instead.
